Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NexMart Inc. Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up for questions will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NexMart Inc.'s fourth quarter and full year 2023 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, COO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NexMart Inc.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong fourth quarter and full year 2023 performance, driven by sustained average order value trends amid a mix shift to higher-margin categories and impressive gains in our international markets. 

Our focus remains on navigating seasonality effectively while capitalizing on positive deviations through technology investments. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NexRec AI recommendation platform, which we believe will significantly enhance personalization and upsell opportunities across our global customer base.

Finally, we are committed to delivering on profitability targets, as evidenced by our net income and EPS results that exceeded expectations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our fourth quarter revenue was $8.7 billion, an increase of 18% year-over-year. Gross margin was 28.4%, driven by improved product mix, better inventory turnover, and efficiencies in fulfillment. Operating expenses were $1.67 billion, representing 19.2% of revenue, reflecting disciplined cost controls and cloud migration benefits.

Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.42 per diluted share, marking a 32% increase year-over-year and beating consensus expectations. We ended the quarter with $1.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year 2024 guidance of $35 to $38 billion in revenue, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 12-14%.

As we unpack these results, let me first highlight our average order value—or AOV—trends, a vital metric influencing our take rate, gross merchandise value—or GMV—and our overall profitability in this competitive e-commerce arena. AOV, simply total revenue divided by total orders, helps us scale efficiently without spiking customer acquisition costs, or CAC.

In the fourth quarter, our trailing 12-month AOV hit $142, reflecting an 8% year-over-year rise from around $131 in the prior period, continuing a multi-quarter uptrend with sequential improvement. This contributed roughly $2.8 billion in revenue from AOV expansion alone, surpassing our overall GMV growth. Key drivers included a strategic shift in product mix toward higher-ticket items, where electronics and appliances now make up 28% of GMV, up from 22% last year—similar to dynamics at online arms of big-box retailers. Penetration of baskets over $200 climbed 15% year-over-year, spurred by demand for smart home tech and appliances in the lingering home upgrade cycle. Meanwhile, we trimmed low-AOV fast fashion to 18% of mix from 24%, using AI merchandising to favor premium SKUs, which also lifted gross margins by over 100 basis points.

We supercharged this with AI-driven personalization via our NexRec platform, processing real-time data from most sessions to boost add-to-cart rates by 12% on complementary products—like pairing beauty items with tools, raising category AOV by 18%. Visual search and AR try-ons cut returns and encouraged bigger baskets, especially on mobile, which drives 62% of orders and narrowed its AOV discount to desktop.

Bundling played a big role too, generating hundreds of millions in extra GMV through NexBundle programs for electronics and groceries, where discounted kits averaged much higher values than single items. We adjusted free shipping thresholds regionally—$49 in the US, €45 in Europe, and equivalent in APAC—pushing 14% of carts over without hiking logistics costs.

Regionally, North America, at 55% of GMV, saw the strongest AOV lift to $56 equivalent, thanks to pricing power in durables amid inflation and growth in high-population states. Europe grew more modestly amid energy issues, with gains in Germany offsetting UK flatness via localized strategies. APAC exploded, particularly India and Southeast Asia, where super-app integrations lifted premium bundles.

Headwinds like economic pressures and rival discounting shaved some off, but our NexVIP loyalty program—with 18 million members up 40%—drove higher repeat AOV and lifetime value. Looking ahead, we're aiming for double-digit AOV growth through VIP expansion, generative AI bundles, and new verticals like wellness subscriptions, while stress-testing for downturns.

Shifting to seasonality, which is a classic e-commerce pattern we manage closely: peaks in Q4 from holidays and promotions, softer Q1, mid-year ramps, and holiday build-up. Historically, Q4 has been 42-48% of annual GMV, in line with industry leaders. In FY2023, full-year GMV hit $28.7 billion, up 22%, with Q4 at $13.9 billion—48.5% of the total and up 12% year-over-year, beating benchmarks.

Orders surged 15% to 98 million, powered by loyalty redemptions. However, AOV compressed slightly to $142 from expectations, due to price-matching in apparel against low-cost rivals and value-seeking shifts amid inflation—premium baskets dipped, especially in APAC hit by currency and Singles' Day pull-forward.

Positively, North America boomed with BFCM generating billions, aided by our SmartCart AI for peak conversions. EMEA held strong with localized kits. We've countered seasonality with faster inventory turns at 8.2x via ML forecasting, micro-fulfillment for same-day delivery, and evergreen promotions like Flash Fridays to smooth demand.

For 2024, we're targeting sustained GMV growth by extending peaks year-round, investing in APAC warehouses, and leveraging our marketplace for margin buffers.

International expansion remains central to our strategy, scaling our asset-light model beyond North America. In Q4, these markets were 28% of total GMV, up from 22% a year ago, delivering strong growth that outpaced domestic results and leveraged platform efficiencies.

Europe, our top international region at 42% of that GMV, grew robustly with MAU up 41% to over 15 million and retention at 68%. AOV rose on premium beauty and fashion, enabled by dynamic pricing, local payments, and faster shipping that cut fulfillment costs.

APAC flew high, with Southeast Asia and India leading via super-app features, live-streaming, and low-CAC video ads—mobile orders dominant, LTV up 25% via subscriptions, and edge warehouses slashing delivery times.

LATAM scaled with better take rates, private-label groceries, and drone pilots reducing last-mile expenses. Overall, we added millions of active customers, with GMV per user rising on personalization tech like computer vision search. Contribution margins expanded as CAC fell from organic channels.

We're on pace for major international GMV milestones in 2024, with capex for fulfillment, blockchain for customs, and AI for FX hedging, while focusing on high-LTV areas.

Finally, on the bottom line: Q4 net income of $285 million beat expectations by a wide margin, with EPS at $1.42 topping forecasts 16%. Full-year net income rose 28% to $1.02 billion, EPS $5.10 versus expected $4.75. This stemmed from 22% GMV growth, customer expansion, record repeats via AI recs, margin gains from turnover and mix, and OpEx leverage from tech migrations and optimized networks.

Regionally, North America dominated profits, APAC accelerated, Europe grew despite headwinds. Our flywheel—supply chain investments and data advantages—delivers sector-leading margins. For Q1 2024, we guide EPS above consensus, with 20-25% full-year net income growth.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Instructions for the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Ross with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Ross:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. On AOV, you highlighted some headwinds from economic pressures and competition—can you elaborate on mitigations and how that factors into FY24 outlook?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. Absolutely, while we saw some drag from trade-downs in non-essentials and mobile impulse buys, our tiered loyalty like NexVIP has been key, boosting repeat AOV 25% and LTV significantly. We've also deprioritized low-margin SKUs via AI assortment tools. For FY24, this positions us for 10-12% growth, with new AI pilots targeting 15% lifts and high-AOV vertical entries. We're resilient with 85% repeat rates to grab more wallet share.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Great, thanks. On international expansion, APAC looks explosive but with regulatory and FX risks—how are you addressing those, and what's the capex plan?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. APAC's hypergrowth comes from low CAC via targeted ads and super-app integrations, with strong LTV validation. For risks, we've localized payments like UPI in India, hedged FX with AI forecasting, and invested $500 million in warehouses and edge computing to counter tariffs and geopolitics. Capex totals $300 million for new micro-centers and blockchain customs tools, aiming for 55% international GMV growth to $12 billion annualized, diversified like successful regional players.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan.

David Patel:
Thanks for taking my question. Regarding seasonality, the Q4 deviations from AOV expectations—how are you planning to mitigate similar issues next year, especially in softer regions?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, David. Seasonality is our rocket fuel, but we address deviations operationally through ML demand forecasting that cut stockouts sharply, scaling micro-fulfillment to 45 units for 65% same-day urban delivery, and boosting repeats 11%. For 2024, 'Evergreen Seasonality' via micro-promos and Web3 loyalty will extend peaks, with APAC-specific warehouses to handle comps like Singles' Day. Our marketplace mix provides buffers, targeting 20%+ GMV even if Q4 share moderates slightly.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Seasonality impact: Analyze trends and explain deviations.
International market expansion: Progress and performance metrics.
Net income and earnings per share (EPS): Performance vs. expectations.

aspect_summary.Average order value (AOV) trends: Factor: Trailing 12-month AOV reached $142 (+8% YoY), driven by product mix shift to higher-ticket electronics/appliances (28% GMV from 22%), AI personalization (NexRec boosting add-to-cart 12%, category AOV +18%), bundling, adjusted shipping thresholds, and NexVIP loyalty; headwinds from economic pressures and competition mitigated; targeting double-digit growth in 2024.
aspect_summary.Seasonality impact: Analyze trends and e: Q4 GMV was 48.5% of FY2023 total ($13.9B of $28.7B, +12% YoY), exceeding 42-48% historical norms; orders +15%; AOV compressed slightly due to apparel price-matching, inflation-driven value-seeking, and APAC Singles' Day pull-forward; deviations countered by ML forecasting, 8.2x inventory turns, micro-fulfillment, and evergreen promotions like Flash Fridays; 2024 plans include 'Evergreen Seasonality' for sustained growth.
aspect_summary.International market expansion: Progress: International GMV 28% of total (up from 22% YoY), outpacing domestic; Europe (42% of int'l) MAU +41% to 15M+, 68% retention, AOV gains; APAC explosive via super-apps, live-streaming, subscriptions (LTV +25%); LATAM scaled with better take rates, private-label; added millions of users, GMV/user up, margins expanded, CAC down; 2024 targets 55% growth to $12B annualized with $500M capex for warehouses/blockchain.
aspect_summary.Net income and earnings per share (EPS):: Q4 net income $285M (+32% YoY), EPS $1.42 (beat consensus 16%); FY net income $1.02B (+28%), EPS $5.10 (vs. $4.75 expected); driven by 22% GMV growth, customer/repeat expansion via AI, margin gains from mix/turnover, OpEx leverage; Q1 2024 EPS above consensus, FY 20-25% net income growth.
